title: Spring Data JPA: @Query with the % (modulo) operator fails at startup with 'mismatched input '%''

sources.license: Facts summarized from a public GitHub issue/PR; short error excerpt quoted.

symptom: Creating a repository bean fails with QueryCreationException caused by BadJpqlGrammarException: mismatched input '%' for an @Query such as 'select c from Call c where c.duration % 2 = 0 order by c.id'. The failure happens at startup, before the query is ever run, and Hibernate itself accepts the same HQL.
cause: Spring Data JPA validates @Query strings with its own ANTLR HQL grammar before Hibernate sees them. That grammar allows only * and / as multiplicative operators and has no rule for the % remainder operator, so the query is rejected.
fixSummary: Replace the operator with the standard function: where mod(c.duration, 2) = 0. Moving the query to a native query (nativeQuery = true) or to a Specification/Criteria query also works if the result stays the same. Fixed in Spring Data JPA 4.1.2 (2026.0.2).
